chunks: Mu'āwiyah ibn 'Ammār narrated from Abī 'Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The muhrim removes from himself all vermin, except the louse, for it is from his body. So if he wishes to move a louse from one place to another, it does not harm him.

key_terms.الدَّوَابَّ: creatures or vermin found on the body
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: a person in the state of ihram during hajj or 'umrah
key_terms.فَلَا يَضُرُّهُ: it does not harm him; it brings no legal consequence upon him
key_terms.يُلْقِي: removes or casts off from himself

ai.seo_question: What may a muhrim do with lice and other insects while in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning a person in the state of ihram. It states that the muhrim may remove other creatures from himself, but lice are treated differently, and merely moving a louse from one place to another is not considered harmful in ruling.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2704 - Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"A person in the state of ihram should remove all insects from themselves, except for lice, as they are from their body. However, if they wish to move a louse from one place to another, it does not harm them."
